title: Theo's Power-Up Picnic
markdown:
The sunburst painted Theo’s window gold. He bounced right out of bed, his toes tapping a happy beat. “Today!” he declared. “The Great Forest Treasure Hunt!” Theo loved adventures. He pictured sparkling gems and clever clues. But today was also about picnic power. He, Poppy the dormouse, and Ms. Vale were packing perfect picnic snacks. Snacks that would not quit.

Poppy peeked from her leafy bed. Her whiskers twitched. “A treasure hunt!” she squeaked. “But it’s a big one, Theo. What if my little legs get wobbly? What if I just want to nap?” She imagined herself sitting, the treasure lost.

Theo gave her a quick pat. “No naps, Poppy! We’ll pack super snacks. Power snacks! Energy that lasts and lasts. No poof energy for us!”

Ms. Vale, her library bag gleaming, nodded. “Exactly. We need food that gives steady power, not a quick burst that vanishes. Like a slow river, not a sudden splash.” She gestured to the sunlit kitchen table. “Poppy, what makes you feel strong and ready to keep going?”

Poppy nibbled her lip. “Biscuits are yummy,” she said. “But they make me feel… crumbly. Like an old twig!”

“Ah, biscuits often have lots of sugar,” Ms. Vale said gently. “Sugar gives a quick zoom, like a rocket. But then, poof! The energy is gone. You feel tired.”

Theo tapped his chin. “So we need food that doesn’t go poof?”

“Precisely!” Ms. Vale beamed. “Think of hearty bread. Its energy comes out slowly, like that steady river. It keeps you going. Or apples! They have natural sugar, but also fibre that helps your body use the energy slowly. They keep you full and strong.”

“What about muscles?” Theo flexed. “For climbing trees!”

“Protein,” Ms. Vale announced. “Yogurt or nuts. They build your muscles. They’re like tiny bricks for your body, helping you jump and balance.”

Soon their picnic basket was a rainbow of power-packed foods. Thick wholemeal bread. Crisp juicy apple wedges. Creamy yogurt. Neat bags of nuts.

“This bread,” Theo said, tapping a slice, “will make my legs pump like pistons for dashing.”

Poppy munched an apple wedge. “Sunshine in my mouth!” she chirped. “And a crunch like leaves!”

Ms. Vale packed carefully. “These foods are a team. Grains for steady fuel. Fruit for vitamins and gentle energy. Yogurt and nuts for strength. They’ll power your treasure hunt all day.”

With their basket packed, Theo, Poppy, and Ms. Vale headed for the whispering woods. The air smelled of pine and damp earth. Poppy scampered beside Theo. She felt a quiet strong energy buzzing inside. It made her want to skip.

“This food is amazing!” Poppy chirped, bouncing with every step. “I feel like I could run to the tallest oak and back!”

Ms. Vale chuckled. “That’s the steady power of good food, Poppy. It helps you explore and have fun without getting weary. Just like strong bridges need strong materials, our bodies need good food for energy and strength for any adventure.”

Theo grinned, scanning the path. “And with that steady power,” he declared, “today is going to be spectacular.”

The adventure was just beginning. Theo wondered what other treasures waited if the snacks kept their promise—another clue, another climb, another river of energy that did not go poof.
characters: Theo (bridge builder), Poppy (leafy-bed dormouse), Vale (library-bag teacher)
